cells.tense: Right now the compass sits easy in the hand and points true.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to no one, one thing you are carrying for someone and one thing they carry for you.
cells.core:
You can tell what is fair here without working it out. Somebody says a thing and the truth of it lands in your body ahead of your head, and what you are pointed at is still pointed at. The fairness is not slowing the walking — the reading and the direction are doing their work in the same motion, which is exactly the shape of this going well.

The quiet part is that you keep the accounting to yourself and you keep going. Nobody is sending thanks for that, and you are not owed any. It holds anyway, because where you are going and what you think is right are on the same side. Worth noticing while that is true, since you will not notice it later.
cells.sheetLine: What is fair and where you are going line up.
cells.verb: The private compass weighing what is owed against what is
cells.place: Where momentum is pointed and kept

cells.tense: You are settling accounts that have not been opened yet.
cells.ask: Let one thing stay unweighed until tomorrow. Do not fix the balance — just leave it uneven.
cells.core:
When this works, fairness is a reading you take and then walk on — you see what is owed, you act, and the seeing lets the step land clean. What you have instead is the same sense run ahead of itself: nothing has happened yet and the ledger is already open, the debts already counted. What you will owe, what you will be owed, who came out ahead.

Your momentum is still pointed somewhere, but much of it is running on settlements that have not arrived. That is what a hot compass does — it stops telling fair from unfair and starts running a court. What helps is not more careful counting. It is letting one thing sit there uneven.

cells.tense: The compass has gone quiet, and the walking kept going anyway.
cells.ask: Pick one small wrong in front of you and do one concrete thing about it today — not the whole wrong, one thing.
cells.core:
When fairness is running here, it points the motion — you know what is right, and it is the thing you are headed toward, not a weight you carry along. What you have instead is the motion without the reading: still pointed, still holding direction through resistance, and the sense of what is fair is not in it. You can drive without the compass.

What that looks like is not not-caring. It is the instrument off while the engine runs, which carries you a long way before it stops carrying you. You do not fix it by feeling your way back into the big question. You fix it by acting on one small wrong that is actually in front of you.
cells.sheetLine: You kept moving after the sense of right went quiet.

cells.tense: The compass is drawing the line right now and it is being called something else.
cells.ask: Catch one judgement you make today and say it as yours, out loud: this is wrong.
cells.core:
When this runs clean, you feel the unfairness, you say what you find, and the direction follows the finding — no gap between the call and the walking, and the call has your name on it. What you have instead is the call alone, made and unnamed: you hold the line already, in what you will not do, what you quietly refuse, the thing you will not put up with and have not said so about. It runs clean. It just gets booked as practicality, or as the situation being what it is.

What is missing is whose call it is. One of those calls said out loud as yours costs almost nothing, and once it is yours the direction and the compass work as one thing.
cells.sheetLine: You are drawing the line. You are calling it the situation.
